correctness.rationale: For each Gaussian heat kernel, the twisted periodic heat solution has explicitly positive boundary data by Poisson summation. The Dirichlet heat maximum principle forces a common positive interior imaginary sector. On the half-frequency line a second Dirichlet heat problem gives strict real signs, and Hopf plus the exact Gaussian derivative identity gives nonzero, sign-aligned central Jacobian. Positive integration preserves all strict signs and justified differentiability under the inverse-square-root measure integrability hypothesis. Compact Zak frame fibers have no common zero at integer oversampling. Standalone finite checks completed 4296 comparisons, but are not treated as a universal proof.

value.rationale: Unique regular Zak zeros govern practical Gabor frame design. The theorem holds across the full infinite-dimensional cone of positive Gaussian precision mixtures, rather than a finite family of individually Gaussian windows, and supplies all integer-oversampled frame lattices. The explicit two-scale example violates the standard TP and convexity hypotheses, showing a nontrivial advance in geometric stability under positive mixing. Strict sign sectors and Jacobian orientation are structural, not routine normalization or a tiny numerical increment.
